strategy_title: maxnreg Register Cap Hurts When Spill Dominates
strategy_description: Adding maxnreg to Triton configs reduced registers/thread from 168 to 128 and raised Block Limit Registers from 3 to 4, but achieved occupancy remained stuck at 6.25% — the grid (112 blocks < 132 SMs) was the binding constraint, not register count. The register cap forced the compiler to spill to local memory, introducing uncoalesced local load/store traffic (new MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule, 42.3% speedup potential flagged) and increasing executed instructions by ~15% (16.4M → 18.9M), causing a 24% slowdown. When the kernel is wave-limited (grid_size < sm_count) rather than occupancy-limited, capping registers via maxnreg cannot improve throughput and instead adds spill overhead that degrades performance.
fast_pseudocode:
# After: 128 regs/thread via maxnreg, 4 blocks/SM theoretical
# BUT: achieved occupancy unchanged (6.25%), spill traffic added
@triton.autotune(configs=[
    triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=2, maxnreg=128),
    triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=2, maxnreg=96),
    triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=2, maxnreg=64),
    # ... 11 more configs with maxnreg=128/96/64
], key=[])
applicable_when: Never effective when grid_size < sm_count (wave-limited regime). Only potentially useful when: (1) achieved occupancy is genuinely register-limited (Block Limit Registers is the binding constraint AND grid_size >> sm_count so more blocks can actually run), AND (2) the register spill cost to L2/shared is lower than the occupancy gain benefit.
do_not_apply_when: Grid is wave-limited (grid_size <= sm_count): capping registers cannot increase the number of concurrently running blocks because there are not enough blocks to fill the GPU regardless. Also avoid when the kernel already has significant shared memory bank conflicts — spilled registers go to local memory via L1TEX and add uncoalesced access patterns on top of existing bottlenecks. Profiling signals: waves_per_sm < 1.0 AND grid_size < sm_count → do not apply maxnreg.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: maxnreg is passed as a parameter to triton.Config(). It sets a PTX-level register cap that forces the compiler to spill excess registers to local memory (L1TEX → L2). The spill traffic appears as MemoryCacheAccessPattern NCU warnings with ~1 byte utilized per 32-byte sector. In CUDA, the equivalent is __launch_bounds__(max_threads, min_blocks) or -maxrregcount compiler flag.
